messages:
maya_support: forwarding a support case from AcmeHealth (acct: acct_acme_9876). They triggered 429s overnight and think quota should have reset at local midnight PT. They pasted the API response and X-Quota-Reset header.

acme_rep: we ran a nightly batch around 01:00 PT and started getting 429s at ~05:10 PT. console shows 0 tokens remaining for March. expected reset at 00:00 PT. can you confirm when hosted monthly quotas actually reset?

acme_rep: API payload snippet:
{\n  \"error\": \"quota_exhausted\",\n  \"message\": \"Monthly quota exhausted for account\",\n  \"code\": 429\n}\nResponse headers:\nX-Quota-Remaining: 0\nX-Quota-Reset: 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z\n
maya_support: thanks — triaging. two quick clarifications: 1) are you on the standard hosted plan (not enterprise with custom anchor)? 2) are you using streaming endpoints for those jobs?

acme_rep: standard hosted plan. we do have some streaming jobs but the big batch was non-streaming generation.

sam_engineer: quick answer: hosted monthly quotas are aligned to calendar months in UTC. X-Quota-Reset is authoritative and is an ISO8601 UTC timestamp. If you see X-Quota-Reset: 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z then the quota becomes available exactly at that instant (00:00 UTC on 2026-03-01).

sam_engineer: timezone note (to avoid confusion): 00:00 UTC on the 1st = 16:00 the previous day in PT during standard time (UTC-8) and 17:00 the previous day in PDT (UTC-7). There is no per-account local-midnight reset for hosted accounts; billing invoice timestamps are a separate concern.

jules_billing: confirmed acct_acme_9876 is a hosted-tier account with no custom billing anchor. if this were a dedicated enterprise arrangement we could anchor by signup day, but not in this case.

alex_sre: streaming token accounting: tokens are recorded server-side as the model emits them. If the client disconnects mid-stream you are billed for tokens already emitted. There is no automatic deduplication across retries — if a client retries the same prompt and the model emits tokens again, those are billed anew. Check for retried jobs or duplicate workers picking up the same queue item.

maya_support: customer asked for minimal repro steps to verify the authoritative reset and to observe token consumption for streaming vs non-streaming.

sam_engineer: repro steps to send to customer (minimal, safe):

1) verify account windows and balances:

curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/usage?period=month\" | jq
# look for fields: remaining_tokens, month_start, month_end

2) compare a failing request's X-Quota-Reset header to the month_end returned by usage endpoint. they should match (both ISO8601 UTC).

3) simulate a streaming abort and observe usage delta:

```
# start a streaming request, kill client after a few events
curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" -d '{"prompt":"long-running test","stream":true}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
# kill client (CTRL-C) after some tokens have arrived, then run usage endpoint again to see tokens charged
```

4) check logs for retry loops or job requeues around the time tokens were spent. common causes: cron replay that replays items after a failure window, or multiple workers without idempotency keys.

sam_engineer: also include this small check to ensure headers are reliable:

curl -I -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate | egrep -i \"X-Quota-|\")
# you should see X-Quota-Remaining and X-Quota-Reset. treat X-Quota-Reset as canonical reset timestamp (UTC).

acme_rep: can you do anything now to unblock us? our users are impacted.

jules_billing: we can apply an emergency token adjustment for support cases. I applied +50000 tokens as a temporary top-up: ADJ-20260301-2200, expires 2026-03-05T00:00:00Z. finance approval needed for larger amounts. this adjustment appears under Console > Billing > Adjustments.

billing_bot: [auto] Adjustment ADJ-20260301-2200 applied to acct_acme_9876 by jules_billing (+50000 tokens). Expires: 2026-03-05T00:00:00Z.

acme_rep: thanks — the top-up cleared the 429s. we'll run the repro and follow up.

alex_sre: preventative recommendations to include in reply:
- add idempotency keys to job processing so retries don't double-run the same prompt
- avoid large backfill jobs crossing the UTC month boundary; if unavoidable, split and throttle across the boundary
- enable Console alerts: Console > Settings > Alerts to get email/Slack warnings when remaining_tokens drops below X%
- for programmatic alerts use our usage webhook (beta) or poll /v1/usage hourly

sam_engineer: example webhook payload we send:

{\n  \"account_id\": \"acct_acme_9876\",\n  \"remaining_tokens\": 47000,\n  \"threshold\": 0.1,\n  \"window_end\": \"2026-03-01T00:00:00Z\"\n}

maya_support: action items: 1) jules_billing confirm adjustment (done) 2) send customer repro steps and alert docs (sending now) 3) customer to run repro and ack. i'll follow up in 2 hours.

acme_rep: confirmed tokens came back online at 00:00 UTC and the interim credit resolved immediate issues. we'll implement idempotency and set alerts. thanks! :white_check_mark:

alex_sre: small docs task: i'll add an FAQ blurb \"Why didn't my quota reset at my local midnight?\" to reduce future confusion. filing PR.

maya_support: closing thread after customer ack. if anything else crops up reopen or ping us in #support-escalations.
